docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: • A documentation site at https://clinical-qikit.github.io/qikit/docs/: the guide, the methods, an API reference built from the docstrings, and this changelog. The guide pages are drawn from the README's sections, so the README stays the one copy. Each release tag publishes it; mkdocs build --strict runs in CI.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• funnel() no longer stalls on proportions with a provider far below the center line. The shrunk-estimate interval inverts a beta distribution; when a provider's posterior had a shape near 0, each evaluation ran its continued fraction off the side where it converges, 100,000 terms at a time, and a funnel could take minutes. Each tail now comes from the fraction that converges at that point; values agree with the previous ones to 1e-11 and no snapshot moved.
  • A proportion funnel's upper limits stop at 1. When the providers spread wider than any beta distribution allows, the limits fall back to the published normal formula, whose upper contour could pass 1 (2.34 in one case); the lower contour was already stopped at 0.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Property-based tests (tests/test_properties.py, Hypothesis): rules that hold for any input rather than one example, such as limits nesting around the center line, a change of units moving the I chart and keeping its signals, freeze= ignoring later points, each part= being its own chart, a funnel ignoring the order of providers, excluding a provider being the same as leaving it out, and an incomplete row being dropped and counted. They found both fixes above.
  • CI runs on Python 3.14.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• funnel(exclude=7) takes a single unit id, as qic(exclude=) does; it raised TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable. exclude=True now says it wants ids or a column name.
  • Without data=, a hover= entry named like a result column is refused. With hover={"numerator": [...]} the hover values silently replaced the numerator column in result.data; it now raises, as it already did with data=.
  • Without data=, unit= or label= as a string is refused. It was read as a sequence of letters (label="name" labelled four providers n, a, m, e); it now says to pass a sequence.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: • tests/conformance_helpers.py is gone. The Python tests use qic() and funnel() directly; tests/fixture_adapter.py (311 lines, from 447) runs the shared fixtures in the TypeScript engine's vocabulary, and tests/test_fixture_adapter.py pins the parts of that vocabulary that are not simply new names.

docs.title: Excel add-in
docs.text:
• A privacy and security page is published with the add-in (privacy.html beside the task pane) and set as the JSON manifest's privacy URL. It covers what is loaded and from where, what is read and written in the workbook, and how to review or pin a version.
  • A Content Security Policy on every published page: scripts only from the add-in's folder and Office.js's hosts, no eval, no frames, and network requests only to the add-in's folder and Office.js's. npm run build fails if a page lacks it.
  • Copy details on every error. Each panel's error message, and the crash screen, offer Copy details: the add-in and Excel versions, the panel, the message, the Office.js error code and the trace, ready to paste into an issue. Nothing is sent. Office.js error codes were previously dropped when the add-in reworded the message.
  • A public demo: latest/demo.html runs the task pane against a sample workbook in any browser.
  • Component tests: the four panels are tested end to end through the demo's mock workbook (jsdom and Testing Library), including errors and the crash screen.

docs.title: Fixed (Excel add-in)
docs.text:
• The Bernoulli CUSUM panel picks the 0/1 column. With an ID column first, it used the IDs and failed with "Target must be between 0 and 1". It now starts on the first column of 0s and 1s, and a column with other values gets a message saying what the panel needs. Blank cells are skipped; they were counted as 0 (no event).
  • The task pane works in Excel. Since 1.4.2 the published task pane also loaded the browser demo's mock of Office.js, which replaced Excel's own: in Excel the pane showed the demo with made-up data and never read or wrote the workbook. The demo is now a separate page, demo.html, and npm run build fails if the task pane's scripts contain the mock. Opened in a browser, the task pane now says it runs in Excel and links to the demo.

docs.title: Excel add-in
docs.text:
• An XML manifest is published beside the app package (manifest.xml in latest/ and each version folder), generated from manifest.template.xml and checked by Microsoft's validator in CI and before publishing. It is for installing without an administrator where Teams uploads are turned off: "Upload My Add-in" in Excel, or sideloading on Mac and Windows. docs/deployment.md describes each route and how to tell whether an organization has blocked it.
  • The SPC panel says what it found. Under the chart, a verdict and a sentence per finding ("A shift: 12 points in a row below the center line, Jan 2026 to Dec 2026.", points outside the limits by name, too few crossings), and the Python notes word for word when fewer than 12 points set the center line or fewer than 20 set the limits.
  • Try with sample data. The empty SPC panel offers a made-up, labelled two-year monthly series on a new sheet, so a new user sees a chart and a finding at once.
  • Help me choose. Up to two plain questions (a measurement or a count; which kind of denominator, or one value or an average) pick the chart, defaulting to a run chart when unsure. Choosing a P or U chart without its denominator now says which box to fill.
  • Settings are remembered per workbook (chart type, data grain, rules and limit options, include source data), saved in the workbook once you change one.

docs.title: Fixed (Excel add-in)
docs.text:
• Dates in Excel are recognized as dates. Excel hands date cells to an add-in as serial numbers, so a real date column was read as numbers and could not set the x-axis or be grouped by month. Columns are now classified by their number format; date text is recognized only when it looks like a date ("Ward 3" and "3" no longer do). The reporting period follows the data's spacing, so daily data is no longer folded into months by default.
  • Rows that cannot be used are listed, not silently dropped, with the sheet row and the reason (no value, not a number, no date, no denominator, denominator 0).
  • A missing denominator is never read as zero. By date, a row with no denominator added its count but nothing to the total, inflating that period's rate; elsewhere one bad denominator dropped the whole denominator column.
  • Labels, notes and included source data stay with their points when rows are left out; they shifted by one for every skipped row. Live updates read formats too.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• One-factor-at-a-time designs are analyzed as what they are. analyze() applied the factorial formula to design_type="one_factor", whose runs are not balanced, so every effect was wrong (in a three-factor example an effect of 4 came out as −7.75, with interactions that such a design cannot estimate). Each effect is now the mean with that factor high minus the mean of the baseline runs, which is the least-squares fit. Only main effects are reported, and ss and pct_contribution are NaN because the terms do not partition the total. The Excel engine has the same fix (shared fixture effects_one_factor) and writes those two cells blank.
  • plot("cube") draws two-factor experiments as a square with the mean response at each corner, where it showed "coming soon". One factor raises, naming chart="single_factor".
  • plot("line_effects") is in standard order, as its title says. It plotted the response in run order, which is a different chart once the design is randomized. Replicates follow in turn and center points come last; hover shows each run's number.

docs.title: Excel add-in
docs.text:
• Installable without the repository. Each release tag publishes the task pane to GitHub Pages under vX.Y.Z/ and latest/, each with an app package (qikit-excel-addin.zip) for the Microsoft 365 admin center or Teams custom-app upload. docs/deployment.md is rewritten around those routes, self-hosting, and a privacy statement.
  • Production manifest. The unified manifest moves from the devPreview schema to 1.29, with a GUID, hosted URLs, the 192 px and outline app icons, an 80 px ribbon icon, a tooltip, and an ExcelApi 1.7 requirement (chart series and the series axis). It is generated from manifest.template.json; the committed manifest.json is the dev manifest ("QI Kit (dev)", its own id). CI builds the add-in and checks both manifests with Microsoft's validator and the published schema.
  • The task pane shows its version, which is the Python package's.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: • docs/snowflake.md named the 1.1.0 wheel in its PUT and IMPORTS lines; it now names the current one, and a test fails when the version moves on without it. The stored procedure and UDTF in that doc are now run by the tests, which check that the UDTF returns the columns its RETURNS TABLE clause declares. Faceted-funnel timings are added to the performance table.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The plot, app and dev extras now require plotly>=5.21. They declared 5.15, but the charts use trace zorder, which plotly added in 5.21; on an older plotly .plot() raised ValueError: Invalid property ... 'zorder'. The tables never needed plotly and are unaffected.
  • One-sided funnel p-values were reversed where the normal model stood in for the exact one (summary["p_value_method"] == "normal"). With worse="higher" or "lower" the provider furthest in the bad direction got the largest p-value, not the smallest, so signal="fdr" could miss it and p_value/q_value were wrong for every provider on that funnel. This arises only when the exact model is unavailable: a proportion funnel whose spread is wider than any beta distribution allows, or over-dispersed counts in the millions. Two-sided p-values (worse unset) and the limits themselves were always correct.
  • design(...).fill(...).plot("timeseries") raised a TypeError from an argument qic() no longer takes.
  • ExperimentDesign.to_json() wrote NaN, which is not JSON, for the unfilled Response column; it and to_dict() now give null/None.
  • Center points no longer shrink the effects of an experiment. analyze() divided each contrast by every run, center points included, so a 2×2 with an A effect of 13 reported 8.67 once two center points were added. Effects, sums of squares and pct_contribution now come from the factorial runs alone, which is the least-squares fit; designs without center points are unchanged. The Excel engine had the same formula and has the same fix, with a shared fixture (effects_center_points).
  • design(randomize="within_blocks") with center points mixed the replicates. The block length counted the center points, so blocks straddled replicates. Each replicate is now shuffled on its own and the center points stay at the end.
Minimum denominators from a reliability target. Additive; no result changes.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• result.min_denominator(reliability=0.7) on funnel() results: the denominator at which a provider's reliability reaches a target (one or several), in the units of n=, with its range from the 95% interval for τ, the number of providers at or above and below it (n_above, n_below), the volume they hold, and each row as a sentence (note). It agrees exactly with the reliability column. When the data show no spread between providers there is no floor, and the result says so.
  • funnel_rollup(data, units=[...], reliability=0.7, ...): the same table for each level of a hierarchy (physician, group, hospital), each fitted separately, for deciding the level at which small providers are rolled up.
  • summary["estimate_tau_ci"]: the profile-likelihood 95% interval for the spread the estimate columns use (estimate_tau). None when tau= is given.
  • skills/minimum-denominators/SKILL.md and a "Minimum denominator recipe" in AGENTS.md: what an agent asks (measure, level, peer group, use, period), calls and reports when asked for a minimum denominator or a rollup level.
Messy input no longer becomes a silent wrong answer, and results gain a predictable, compact surface for pipelines and agents. Nothing is removed.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• qikit.schema("qic" | "funnel"): every column result.data can hold, with its type, whether every call produces it, and its meaning. It is now the single source of the column lists.
  • result.to_table() on qic() and funnel() results: .data with every schema column, in schema order and with fixed types (nullable booleans and integers, strings as objects), empty where the call did not produce it; the facets= columns first and the hover= columns last. The shape a database table or a Snowpark RETURNS TABLE clause needs, whatever options the call used.
  • result.brief(digits=4, limit=25): what was found as a small JSON-safe dict: the verdict or counts, the notes, and only the flagged points (the most recent) or providers (outliers first, then by p-value). About 1 KB where to_json() is tens.
  • result.facet_summary(): the summary as a table, one row per facet, with the same columns faceted or not.
  • to_dict(digits=) and to_json(digits=): round every number to that many significant figures. Default unchanged.
  • Choices ignore case and surrounding spaces (measure="OE", signal=" FDR "), and a misspelt choice or keyword suggests the closest: measure must be one of ..., got 'proportions'. Did you mean 'proportion'?; qic() got an unexpected keyword argument 'charts'. Did you mean 'chart'?.
  • The signatures spell out the choices as Literal types (chart, method, measure, worse, signal, tau_method, benchmark, compare_to, agg_fun), so help(), editors and type checkers show them.
  • bchart(x, ..., data=) takes a column name, as paretochart() does. It now refuses values that are not 0/1 and a baseline= outside the cases, in place of a confusing error or a silent pass.
  • print() of a paretochart() or bchart() result says what was found.
  • qic() summary["notes"] and summary["provisional"]: sentences to show a reader (fewer than 12 baseline points, control limits from fewer than 20, points with no value, a frozen baseline), as funnel() already had; provisional is True under 12 baseline points. Faceted, the notes are prefixed by facet. print(result) shows them.
  • Column-name errors list the columns and suggest the closest, ignoring case, in qic(), funnel() and paretochart(): y='deaths' is not a column of data. Did you mean 'DEATHS'?. funnel()'s message changes from "must name a column of data".

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• funnel() read a missing value as zero. A provider whose y was missing was summed to 0 events and could be flagged a low outlier. A row missing y, n or unit is now left out of the sums and counted in the new summary["n_rows_dropped"], with a note; a provider with no complete row is listed with no value and is not tested. A missing denominator no longer raises "events but a zero denominator", and rows with a missing unit are no longer dropped unannounced.
  • qic() charted Python date objects in row order. Snowpark's to_pandas() returns a DATE column as datetime.date objects, which were treated as text and left unsorted, so limits and run rules were computed on shuffled time. They are now sorted like any other date, and .data["x"] keeps the date objects.
  • qic() turned text that is not a number into a gap. "x" or "n/a" in y, n or target now raises a ValueError showing the values; funnel() and bchart() give the same message in place of a raw numpy error. None, NaN, blank text, numeric text and Decimals are read as before.

  • A handful of points was called stable. print(qic(y=[5])) no longer says "the process looks stable".

  • to_json() raised on Python date values in x and Decimal unit ids, as Snowpark returns DATE and NUMBER columns. Dates serialize as ISO text, Decimals as numbers.

  • A faceted qic() summary lacked the top-level runs_signal.
  • qic()'s docstring did not document the special_cause column.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
Every funnel() result is unchanged, bit for bit.

  • The pure maths moved out of funnel.py into core/: core/shrinkage.py (the prior, shrunk estimates, posterior intervals and P(worse), now one pass instead of two), core/benchmark.py (the achievable benchmark and minimum sufficient denominator), and the pooled center and fixed-center gap test into core/dispersion.py. The within_dispersion readers, which work on pandas rows, are in the new within.py. funnel.py goes from 1,790 lines to about 1,400, and its helpers take one fitted-model object instead of nine to eleven arguments.
  • Warnings are attributed to the caller's line wherever in the package they arise.
  • multiply= in qic() and tau= in funnel() share one number check; qic()'s message is now "multiply must be a number > 0".

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• compare_to= on funnel(): names which question the chart answers. "peers": the pooled center line and overdispersion=True (the default settings). "model": O/E against the risk model's expected, center=1.0 and overdispersion=False; measure="oe" only, and a proportion or rate is told to pass center=<target>, overdispersion=False. A center= or overdispersion= that contradicts it is an error naming the fix; agreeing values are allowed. summary["compare_to"] records "peers", "model" or "custom" on every call, and print(result) ends its first line with the question. Passing compare_to= adds a note saying which question the chart answers. funnel_sensitivity() forwards "peers" and rejects "model", whose runs would all be the same chart.
  • overdispersion= now defaults to None (meaning True unless compare_to="model"), so an agreeing value can be told from an unset one. Every existing call resolves as before.
  • A warning for a fixed center under the spread allowance: center= with overdispersion=True let τ̂ absorb any system-wide gap between the providers and the center, silently widening every limit (center=1.0 on a system running 10% above its risk model nearly quadrupled τ̂). When the gap is beyond chance (p < 0.001, a sandwich-variance t test) and widens the limits at the median volume by at least 10%, funnel() raises a UserWarning and adds a note with the gap, the widening and the fix. New summary keys center_gap, center_gap_p and tau_pooled. Skipped under a pre-specified tau=. Calibrated by scripts/simulate_center_gap.py: at most 0.4% false warnings in any cell; methods §4.2.1, §5.
  • README, the docstring, AGENTS.md (a new funnel decision recipe, with a canonical physician LOS vs Vizient expected call and scorecard-wide FDR), the provider-funnels skill and llms.txt now pair "against the risk model" with compare_to="model" rather than center=1.0 alone. The README's "identical when τ̂ = 0" now says it holds around the pooled center only.

  • Python only; the Excel add-in does not draw funnels.

  • measure="mean" on funnel(): compares providers on a per-case amount, such as EHR minutes per discharge or cost per case, in the amount's own units. Pass one row per case (y= the amount; n= may be omitted), or SQL totals (y=SUM, n=COUNT(*), sum_sq=SUM(y*y)). The center line is the pooled mean, and cases are on the x axis. It is the quasi-Poisson model with within_dispersion always estimated, so every option applies: worse=, signal="fdr", tau_method, max_case_y=, benchmark="eb", facets= and multiply=. It gives exactly the result of the earlier workaround (each case ÷ the pooled mean as O/E, then multiply=), without the rescaling. Methods §4.19.

  • summary["case_sd"]: the SD of a single case, in y's units.
  • Amounts must be ≥ 0. A scalar within_dispersion, cases= and max_case_n= are refused under "mean", because n already is the case count and a single case's denominator is 1.
  • n= is now optional in the signature; every other measure still requires it.
  • The benchmark= docs now say which option suits which measure: "abc" for proportions, "eb" for "oe", "rate" and "mean".
  • Python only; the Excel add-in does not draw funnels.
  • Shrunk estimates with a range, and a caterpillar plot: new columns eb_low and eb_high, an equal-tailed interval for each provider's true value from its exact posterior (gamma on counts, beta on proportions, on effective counts), with interval= (default 0.95), and estimate_flag: "worse", "better" or "no different" ("higher"/"lower" without worse=) as the interval lies against the reference. estimate_flag answers "clearly worse than the reference?", where signal answers "unusual?"; signal is unchanged. No interval and a note when there is no measurable spread. result.plot(kind="caterpillar") draws them: providers sorted by eb_rate, intervals colored by estimate_flag, raw values faint, the reference dotted, small multiples per facet, and top=/bottom= for long lists. New summary keys reference and estimate_tau. Methods §4.14, §5.
  • The estimate columns' prior now uses the ML τ̂ (or tau=) whatever tau_method the limits use, so eb_rate, eb_excess, reliability, prob_worse and benchmark="eb" values change. The published estimator understates τ: under it 95% intervals covered 49–89% of true values, under ML 91–95%. Limits, p-values, q-values and signal are unchanged. An ML τ̂ that would leave every provider's reliability below 0.01 counts as no spread.
  • Shrinkage against the risk model: under compare_to="model" (and the equivalent center=1.0, overdispersion=False) the estimate columns, which were empty, now use a prior centered on the pooled value with τ̂ around it, and judge each provider against 1.0. tau= is accepted there and sets only that spread. Limits and flags are unchanged.
  • New core helpers gamma_quantile and beta_quantile (no new dependencies).
  • docs/examples/hierarchical_readmissions.ipynb: the patient-level hierarchical model in PyMC beside funnel(), with an optional hospital level. On its simulated data the two agree to a correlation of 0.996.
  • With within_dispersion the intervals cover about 90%, not 95% (methods §5).
  • Cited: Keenan 2008, Dimick 2010, Marshall & Spiegelhalter 1998, Goodwin 2013, Jones & Spiegelhalter 2011; README physician section now cites Hofer 1999 and Goodwin 2013.

  • Python only; the Excel add-in does not draw funnels.

  • color_by="fdr" on FunnelResult.plot(): colors the points by their q-value tiers (outlier q < fdr_levels[0], alert q < fdr_levels[1]) on a signal="limits" result. The signal column and the drawn 95% and 99.8% lines are unchanged; the legend and caption state the q rule. A figure can now match an action list built from q_value without recoloring traces by name.

  • fdr_watch= (e.g. 0.20) adds a pale, open-diamond watch tier for q below it, on the figure only. It has a watch role in styles=.
  • README, methods §4.11 and the provider-funnels skill now say that under signal="limits" a point beyond the 95% line can have a large q-value.
  • Python only; the Excel add-in does not draw funnels.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• benchmark= on funnel(): a goal the best providers already reach, drawn as a dashed line, with benchmark_share= (default 0.10) defining "the best". Both need worse=; methods §4.18.
  • "abc": Kiefe and Weissman's achievable benchmark of care. Providers are ranked by (x + 1)/(n + 2), and the best are pooled until they hold 10% of patients, ties included. It reproduces GAMUT's worked example. It reports the providers who set it and their volumes, and the minimum sufficient denominator (whose exact rule reproduces Kiefe's Table 3). It also gives the ABC without providers below that denominator (Hall et al. 2013).
  • "eb": the 90th percentile of the shrunk eb_rate toward the better side (O'Brien et al. 2008), for outcome measures.
  • summary["benchmark"] is one dict: method, share, value, and under "abc" providers, coverage, group_denominator, msd, n_below_msd and without_small. The columns are benchmark, meets_benchmark, and benchmark_group under "abc".
  • Python only. The TypeScript engine and the Excel add-in do not have it yet.

1.0 is a breaking release. qic() and funnel() now share one vocabulary, display options moved to .plot(), the package imports without plotly, and both functions were checked against R (qicharts2, FunnelPlotR, NHSRplotthedots). Every removed or renamed argument raises a TypeError naming its replacement, so running an app once lists the changes to make.

docs.title: Breaking: calling qic() and funnel()
docs.text:
• Keyword-only after data. qic(data=None, *, x=None, y, n=None, chart="run", ...) and funnel(data=None, *, y, n, measure, ...). A positional qic(x, y) call raises.
  • Display options moved to .plot(): title, subtitle, caption, xlab, ylab, styles, label_signals, x_range, y_range, show_legend, width, height on both, plus x_log on funnels and part_labels, show_95, show_labels, show_grid, show_x_labels, decimals, point_size, x_format, x_angle, x_pad, x_order, y_expand, y_neg, y_percent, connect, runs_highlight, flip, nrow, ncol and scales on qic().
  • Renamed arguments:
Old New Where cl= center= both point_labels= label= both hover_extra= hover= both test_min_expected= fdr_min_denominator= funnel() signal_side= worse= funnel() signal_method= signal= funnel() levels= limits= funnel()
  • Removed: print_summary, y_percent_accuracy and strip_horizontal (no effect), and the hidden chart="ip" (an i chart of a rate is chart="i", y=events, n=cases).
  • facets= takes one column or a list on both functions. The facet columns lead .data under their own names.

docs.title: Breaking: results
docs.text:
• qic() columns. sigma_signal (bool) is now signal ("outlier" or "none"), the same column a funnel has. runs_signal now marks only the points that form a pattern (0.10's runs_signal_localized); too few crossings is summary["crossings_signal"].
  • qic() summary. run_signal is longest_run_signal, run_threshold is longest_run_max, crossings_threshold is n_crossings_min, and limit_basis is gone. New: chart, method, n_outlier, runs_signal, and per-method keys.
  • funnel() summary. phi_raw and phi_debiased are one key, phi, as the chosen tau_method defines it. test_min_expected is fdr_min_denominator. New: limit_method, tau_scale, min_detectable_median.
  • Every result has to_dict() and to_json(). FunnelResult lives in qikit.results with the others.

docs.title: Breaking: packaging and modules
docs.text:
• plotly is optional. pip install "clinical-qikit[plot]" for .plot(). The core depends only on numpy and pandas, and import qikit does not load plotly. .plot() without plotly raises an ImportError naming the extra.
  • Modules. qikit.spc (a package) and qikit.render are gone. The numeric core is qikit.core (dist, constants, shewhart, rules, contours, dispersion, pvalues, power); the front doors are qikit.spc (a module) and qikit.funnel; figures are qikit.plot. Import from qikit itself; the internal paths are not API.

docs.title: Behavior changes
docs.text:
Each moves results on some data. "More" or "less sensitive" is relative to 0.10.

  • tau_method="spiegelhalter" is the default again, in both engines. 0.10's debiased default was not sensitive enough for screening in production use: it found a planted outlier 38% of the time against 70% (methods §5, K = 150, τ = 0.3). The published estimator is also uncorrected like the CQC, NHS and FunnelPlotR estimators. Flag rates return to 0.9's. "winsorized" remains for when the stated chance-flag rate must hold. More sensitive.
  • Run-chart rule (anhoej) matches qicharts2: longest run > round(log₂ n) + 3, and no minimum n. 0.10 used floor(log₂ n) + 3 with ≥. Less sensitive: in simulation false signals fall from 2–10% to 0–2%, and power to see a 1 SD shift falls from 37% to 13% at n = 30. The crossings rule is unchanged. method="nhs" or "ihi" restore a shorter run under a published rule set.
  • xbar and s charts take their spread from the baseline and each part, honouring freeze=, part= and exclude=. More sensitive after a real change.
  • g chart limits come from the mean, with the median drawn as the centre line (Montgomery, qicharts2). Limits about 10–15% wider. Less sensitive.
  • Laney σ_z is screened at 3.267·MR̄ and no longer floored at 1. Narrower limits on under-dispersed series.
  • method="ihi" uses Provost and Murray's run-chart rules (shift 6, trend 5) on run charts, adds 2 of 3 beyond 2σ and 15 within 1σ on Shewhart charts, and passes over repeated values in a trend. More sensitive.
  • n= divides y on every chart, as in qicharts2. p and pp upper limits are capped at 1; the MR chart's lower limit is 0; a moving range across a part boundary is NaN.
  • Grouped x is sorted when numeric or a date, so runs and moving ranges follow time.
  • c₄ is exact (from the gamma function), not a table. A₃, B₃ and B₄ follow it. Differences are in the fourth significant figure.
  • A fixed center= counts K degrees of freedom in "winsorized"'s τ̂², not K − 1. τ̂² is smaller by about 1/K.
  • An estimated within-dispersion below 1 (binary-outcome O/E from case rows) is kept and labelled as the binomial-variance correction, not floored.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• method="nhs": NHS England's Making Data Count rules on qic(), with variation and special_cause per point, summary["variation"], and summary["assurance"] against target=. Plot colours for improving, concerning and neutral special causes. Checked against NHSRplotthedots.
  • tau_method="cqc" and "shmi": CQC and NHS SHMI over-dispersion on the √, arcsine or log scale, as FunnelPlotR computes them, with limits drawn on that scale and mapped back (limit_method="transformed_normal"). Methods §4.17.
  • funnel_sensitivity(): one row per provider with its tier under each τ option and a consistent flag.
  • Reference tests against R. fixtures/reference/ holds 31 cases from qicharts2, FunnelPlotR and NHSRplotthedots, regenerated by scripts/make_reference_fixtures.R; tests/test_reference.py checks them to 1e-6, with each departure listed.
  • Validation: y < 0, y > n on proportions, center out of range, freeze, part, method, agg_fun, and facet names that collide with output columns.
  • Documentation for people and agents: docs/qic-methods.md, docs/snowflake.md, src/qikit/AGENTS.md (shipped in the wheel), llms.txt, and the skills/spc-monitoring skill. py.typed marks the package as typed.
  • tests/test_docs.py: every argument, quoted value, summary key and column named in the README, AGENTS.md, llms.txt, the skills and the methods docs is checked against the code, and the skills' column lists are checked in both directions.

docs.title: Fixed (funnel())
docs.text:
• exclude= is honoured by within_dispersion="estimate" and the clustering check.
  • expected_false_flags["alert"] counts the alert tier only, under both signal= modes.
  • Above 10⁵ expected events, the limits and p-values both use Byar's approximation and summary["limit_method"] says "byar".
  • max_case_y=/max_case_n= drop the worst case only on the provider's own side of the line.
  • Docstrings for reliability and the p-values corrected.

docs.title: Fixed (.plot())
docs.text: • A chart with part= and text x values (dates read from a CSV) no longer crashes when drawing the part labels.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
Case 0.10 1.0 Proportion funnel, 2,000 providers 3.6 s 0.42 s Proportion funnel, 5,000 providers 10 s 1.1 s O/E funnel, 5,000 providers 0.47 s 0.2 s

Exact binomial intervals and detectability use safeguarded Newton steps on the log tail, about five CDF evaluations instead of fifty. The distribution cache evicts least recently used entries instead of clearing. .plot() and limits() reuse the contours computed for the table.

docs.title: TypeScript engine
docs.text: The Excel add-in's engine matches every behaviour change above: the Anhøj thresholds, ihi rules, exact c₄, g, MR, p and Laney limits, and the tauMethod default. The shared fixtures in fixtures/spc/ were regenerated.

docs.title: Behavior change
docs.text: • The over-dispersion estimate is debiased by default, in both engines (tau_method="winsorized"). The 10%-winsorized φ̂ is multiplied by its Gaussian consistency factor 1.4735 (Spiegelhalter 2005, eq. 9) before τ² is estimated. τ̂ is larger, the adjusted contours are wider, and fewer average providers flag. Without the factor, at 1,000 physicians (E from 2 to 60), τ̂ was 0 for a true spread of 0.10, and average providers flagged at about twice the stated rate. On the bundled example (data/examples/physician_mortality_oe.csv, three years) τ̂ goes from 0 to 0.113, and the same three physicians are outliers. tau_method="spiegelhalter" reproduces 0.9 (and FunnelPlotR/CQC) exactly. The engine core, qic() on O/E charts and the TypeScript engine (tauMethod) use the same default. The shared fixtures that check Spiegelhalter's published numbers now pin tauMethod: "spiegelhalter", and three new fixtures (funnel_*_winsorized) check the default in both engines. See docs/methods.md §4.3.

docs.title: Added (funnel())
docs.text:
• tau_method=: "winsorized" (default), "spiegelhalter" (as published) or "ml" (maximum likelihood of the chart's own random-effects model, with a profile-likelihood tau_ci). tau=: a τ fixed in advance (a number, or one per facet). Summary keys tau_method, tau_source, tau_estimated, tau_ci; notes below 30 providers and when a fixed τ has drifted from this period's estimate (§4.16).

  • prob_worse column: the posterior probability that a provider is worse than average (the CMS question), alongside signal (unusual among peers) (§4.14, §4.16).

  • reliability, eb_rate, eb_excess, raw_excess columns: shrinkage by the exact posterior mean of the chart's own Poisson–gamma or beta-binomial model (§4.14).

  • p_value_drop1, flag_survives_drop1, fragility columns: single-case robustness (§4.15). max_case_y=/max_case_n= supply the worst case from SQL.
  • cases=/sum_sq=: within_dispersion="estimate" and the clustering check from one row per provider aggregated in SQL; equal to the stay-level result to rounding (§4.12).
  • within_dispersion="<column>": one φᵢ per provider (e.g. case-mix weighted by DRG); adds effective_denominator, the plot's x axis (§4.12).
  • test_min_expected=: a volume floor for the false discovery rate step only (independent filtering) (§4.11).
  • Summary keys phi_raw, phi_debiased, test_min_expected, n_filtered, n_fragile, and notes for fragile flags and filtering.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: • dist.py walks are vectorised with strictly sequential numpy accumulations and cached per distribution. Every value is bit-identical to 0.9. A 1,000-provider oep funnel at E from 30 to 2,000 takes about 0.3 s cold, down from 1.3 s. scipy is not required. Monkeypatches of the removed qikit.spc.dist.poisson_cdf have had no effect since 0.8 and can be deleted.

docs.title: Evaluated and declined
docs.text: These are recorded in docs/methods.md §6 with reasons: per-provider own-variance continuous_oe, q_value_loo, Storey/power-screened FDR, winsorized/median center lines, and smoothed display contours.

docs.title: Installing QI Kit for Excel
docs.text: QI Kit for Excel is a task pane add-in. The task pane is a static web page hosted on GitHub Pages; Excel loads it from there. Installing the add-in means giving Excel a manifest that points at that page.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Microsoft 365 (subscription) Excel:

  • Excel on the web
  • Excel on Windows, version 2501 or later
  • Excel on Mac, version 16.103 or later

Perpetual Office (Office 2019, 2021, 2024, LTSC), iPad and phones are out of scope.

docs.title: What is published
docs.text:
Each release vX.Y.Z publishes two copies of the add-in:

Folder Changes Use it to https://clinical-qikit.github.io/qikit/latest/ on every release get fixes without doing anything https://clinical-qikit.github.io/qikit/vX.Y.Z/ never pin a version your organization has reviewed

Each folder holds:

  • qikit-excel-addin.zip: the app package (manifest plus two icons), for the admin center and Teams.
  • manifest.json: the manifest inside that package, for reading.
  • manifest.xml: the same add-in as an add-in-only (XML) manifest, for installing without an administrator (below).
  • the task pane itself (index.html, scripts, icons). Opened in a browser it says it runs in Excel and links to the demo.
  • demo.html: the task pane against a mock workbook, to try in a browser without Excel: https://clinical-qikit.github.io/qikit/latest/demo.html.

docs.title: Install for an organization (Microsoft 365 admin center)
docs.text:
This is the route Microsoft recommends for distributing an add-in inside a tenant, and it needs a Microsoft 365 administrator.

  1. Download qikit-excel-addin.zip from latest/ or from a pinned vX.Y.Z/ folder.
  2. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Settings → Integrated apps → Upload custom apps.
  3. Upload the zip and choose who gets it: specific users, groups, or everyone.
  4. Users find QI Kit as a tab on the Excel ribbon. It may not appear immediately; closing and reopening Excel helps.

With the latest/ package, new releases reach users automatically: the manifest points at latest/, so the task pane updates with no new upload. With a pinned package, users stay on that version until an administrator uploads a newer pinned package.

docs.title: Install for yourself
docs.text:
Many organizations, hospitals especially, turn off installing add-ins without IT. Each route below depends on a different setting, so one may work where another is blocked. If none does, ask IT to use the admin center route above.

Teams upload (uses qikit-excel-addin.zip). In Teams, open Apps → Manage your apps → Upload an app → Upload a custom app and choose the zip, then open Excel. If there is no Upload an app button, or it offers only Submit an app to your org (which sends it to IT for approval), personal uploads are off.

Upload in Excel (uses manifest.xml). In a workbook, Home → Add-ins → More Add-ins → My Add-ins → Upload My Add-in, and choose manifest.xml from latest/. If More Add-ins is greyed out with a workbook open and you signed in, your organization has turned this off.

Sideload on a Mac (uses manifest.xml). Save manifest.xml into ~/Library/Containers/com.microsoft.Excel/Data/Documents/wef (create the wef folder if it is missing) and restart Excel.

Sideload on Windows (uses manifest.xml). This is the developer route Microsoft's tools use; it needs no admin rights but works around the add-in settings above, so check your organization's policy first. Save manifest.xml somewhere on the computer, then in Command Prompt:

reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Office\16.0\WEF\Developer" /v a3880040-4930-41dc-8eab-b2f2c56252e8 /t REG_SZ /d "C:\path\to\manifest.xml"

Restart Excel. To remove it, delete that registry value. An organization that blocks web add-ins entirely blocks this too.

In every route the QI Kit tab appears on the ribbon and the task pane loads from latest/, so it updates with each release.

docs.title: Host it yourself
docs.text:
To keep everything on your own servers (an intranet, Azure Static Web Apps, IIS):

cd excel-addin
npm ci
npm run build
node scripts/manifest.mjs prod https://your.server/qikit/ dist

Copy dist/ to https://your.server/qikit/. The build uses relative paths, so any folder works. The server must use HTTPS with a certificate your users' machines trust. The last command writes dist/manifest.json, dist/qikit-excel-addin.zip and dist/manifest.xml pointing at your URL; distribute them by the routes above.

docs.title: Develop
docs.text:
cd excel-addin
npm install
npm run dev        # HTTPS dev server on https://localhost:3000
npm run sideload   # opens Excel with manifest.json (the dev manifest) installed

Without Excel, open https://localhost:3000/demo.html (or npm run dev:no-https and http://localhost:3000/demo.html) for the task pane against a mock workbook. The mock replaces Office.js's globals when it loads, so only demo.html may import dev-harness.tsx; npm run build fails if the task pane's scripts contain it.

The dev manifest has its own id and is named "QI Kit (dev)", so it installs beside a released copy. manifest.json is generated from manifest.template.json: edit the template, then run npm run manifest. npm run validate checks that manifest.json is current and passes Microsoft's validator and the published schema; CI runs it.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
Pushing a release tag vX.Y.Z (see the root README) runs .github/workflows/addin-pages.yml, which tests, builds, and publishes vX.Y.Z/ and latest/ to the gh-pages branch. The add-in's version is the Python package's version.

One-time setup: in the repository's Settings → Pages, choose Deploy from a branch, branch gh-pages, folder / (root). The branch exists after the workflow's first run. To publish a tag that existed before Pages was enabled, run the workflow by hand with that tag.

docs.title: Privacy and security
docs.text:
The full statement, for users and IT reviewers, is published with the add-in: https://clinical-qikit.github.io/qikit/latest/privacy.html (source: excel-addin/assets/privacy.html). The JSON manifest links to it as its privacy URL (the XML manifest has no such field). In short:

  • QI Kit does all its calculation in the task pane, on your computer. It sends no workbook data anywhere: no requests of its own, no telemetry, no accounts or sign-in.
  • It loads its own files from GitHub Pages (or your server) and Office.js from Microsoft's CDN, nothing else.
  • It reads only the cells you select (and ranges you link for live updates), and writes only to sheets it creates. Its settings live in the workbook.
  • Content Security Policy. Every published page carries one (CSP in excel-addin/vite.config.ts). Scripts may come only from the add-in's folder and Office.js's hosts (appsforoffice.microsoft.com, and ajax.aspnetcdn.com for MicrosoftAjax.js, which Office.js loads). No eval. No frames: this also blocks the telemetry frame Office.js tries to open. Network requests may go only to the add-in's folder, Office.js's CDN, and the virtual host document.localhost that Excel desktop uses. npm run build fails if a page lacks the policy.

If you change what the add-in loads, update the policy and the privacy page together.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Blank task pane: the page did not load. Open the task pane's URL from the manifest in a browser; if it fails there, the hosting is the problem. If it loads in a browser but not in Excel, the Content Security Policy may be blocking something Office.js needs on that platform. Open the task pane's developer tools (right-click → Inspect on Windows, or Safari's Develop menu on Mac) and look for "Content Security Policy" in the console.
  • Something went wrong in a panel: the message has Copy details (versions, panel, error and trace; no cell values). Paste them into an issue.
  • QI Kit tab missing: check the Excel version against the requirements above, then close and reopen Excel. Admin center deployments can take a while to reach users.
  • Old version after a release: GitHub Pages caches pages for a few minutes. Closing and reopening the task pane picks up the new version, shown next to the title.

docs.title: Excel add-in: scope and plan for broad use
docs.text: Written 2026-11-16. Replaces the July 2026 improvement roadmap, whose finished phases are in the git history.

docs.title: Scope: the engine is frozen
docs.text:
The TypeScript engine (excel-addin/packages/engine) does not follow the Python package any further. Python is where new methods go; the add-in is a fixed, supported subset.

In the add-in: run and control charts (run, I, MR, X̄, S, P, U, C, IP, G, T, Laney P′ and U′) with the Anhøj, IHI, WECO and Nelson rules; Pareto charts; Bernoulli CUSUM; two-level designed experiments.

Python only, and staying there: funnel() and everything built on it (p-values and FDR, shrinkage estimates, reliability and minimum denominators, benchmarks, rollups), NHS Making Data Count rules, faceting, and brief()/to_table(). The engine still contains an early funnel mode; it is not shown in the task pane and should not be, since its answers no longer match funnel().

What frozen still requires:

  • The shared fixtures (fixtures/spc, fixtures/experiment) keep passing in both languages. CI runs both.
  • A bug in math the two engines share is fixed in both, in one change, with a fixture.
  • A Python-only feature adds no fixture to the shared directories.

docs.title: Where the add-in stands
docs.text:
Working: four panels, native Excel charts that match the preview, live updates when the source range changes, a browser dev harness, 258 tests, type checks and tests in CI. The production build is about 190 kB gzipped.

What stops someone outside this repository from using it:

  1. Nothing is hosted. The manifest points at https://localhost:3000. There is no published task pane, so installing means cloning the repo and running a dev server.
  2. The manifest is a development one. It is a unified (JSON) manifest on the devPreview schema with a non-GUID id. Microsoft's support table (unified-manifest-overview, October 2026) lists Excel on the web, Windows Microsoft 365 from version 2501 and Mac from 16.103, and says no for perpetual Office on Windows and for mobile. The intended users are all on Microsoft 365, so the JSON manifest is enough once it is on a released schema.
  3. The build is not deployable as it stands. vite build emits the task pane but not the icons or a manifest, and nothing in CI builds or publishes it.
  4. docs/deployment.md describes a different add-in: an XML <SourceLocation> and a taskpane.html that do not exist here.
  5. First-run experience. A new user gets an empty pane and "Use Current Selection". There is no sample data, no guidance on which chart fits their data, and settings are forgotten when the pane closes.
  6. Input handling. Dates are recognized by a serial-number range (25569–60000), so a column of large counts can be read as dates. Dropped non-numeric cells and zero denominators are not reported.
  7. No way to hear about failures, and no privacy statement, which an IT reviewer will ask for. The add-in sends no data anywhere; that needs saying where they will look.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text: Ordered so that each step is usable on its own. Steps 1 and 2 are what "broad use" actually depends on; the rest make it good.

docs.title: 1. Make it installable (about a week)
docs.text:
Built 2026-11-17: .github/workflows/addin-pages.yml, excel-addin/manifest.template.json and scripts/manifest.mjs, rewritten docs/deployment.md. Live once Pages is enabled and a release tag is pushed; the "done when" test below is still to run.

  • Host the task pane on GitHub Pages from a workflow that builds on each release tag and publishes dist/ with the icons. A versioned path per release plus latest, so an organization can pin.
  • Keep the unified (JSON) manifest only and make it a production one: a released schema version instead of devPreview, a real GUID, the hosted URLs, a support URL, and ExcelApi requirement sets that match the APIs used (bindings and chart series need ExcelApi 1.7 or so; confirm by test). Perpetual Office and mobile are out of scope. Revised 2026-11-17: an XML manifest is published too, not for reach but because the JSON package installs only through Teams or the admin center; the XML manifest is what lets one person install it where Teams uploads are blocked.
  • Generate the manifest from one template (dev → localhost, production → Pages) and validate both outputs in CI with office-addin-manifest validate.
  • Rewrite docs/deployment.md around three routes: sideload from the hosted manifest (one person), Microsoft 365 admin center centralized deployment (an organization), and self-hosting dist/ on an intranet.
  • Version the add-in with the package, shown in the task pane footer.

Done when a person with no repository access can install from a URL in five minutes on Windows, Mac and Excel on the web.

docs.title: 2. Make the first five minutes work (about a week)
docs.text:
Built 2026-11-17 for the SPC panel: sample data (a made-up series rather than a data/examples set, since neither monthly example shows a finding), Help me choose, findings and notes, remembered settings, format-based dates and listed skipped rows. The Pareto, CUSUM and experiment panels are unchanged. The "done when" test with a real two-column sheet is still to run in Excel.

  • Sample data. "Try with sample data" writes one of the data/examples sets to a new sheet and charts it. The dev harness already carries the datasets.
  • Chart chooser. Three plain questions (counting events or measuring? is there a denominator? subgroups?) pick the chart type, with the full list still available. Default to a run chart when unsure, as the Python docs advise.
  • Plain-language findings. The summary panel says what was found ("a shift of 9 points below the median starting March") and warns under 12 baseline points, the same wording as Python's summary["notes"].
  • Remember settings per workbook (Office.context.document.settings), with localStorage in the harness.
  • Honest input handling. Use the range's number formats to recognize dates; list the rows that were skipped and why; refuse a zero denominator with a message.

Done when a quality-improvement nurse with a two-column sheet gets a correct chart and a sentence about it without reading documentation.

docs.title: 3. Make it trustworthy to IT and to the next maintainer (several days)
docs.text:
Built 2026-11-17: assets/privacy.html (the JSON manifest's privacy URL), a CSP on every published page (vite.config.ts), Copy details on errors, tests/panels.test.tsx through the demo harness, and the harness published as demo.html. Found on the way: 1.4.2 and 1.4.3 loaded the harness's Office.js mock in Excel (fixed separately, with a build check). The CSP is checked in a browser only; whether Office.js needs more on Windows, Mac or the web is still to confirm in Excel. The end-to-end pass is jsdom rather than a real browser.

  • Privacy and security page: all computation is local to the task pane, no network calls after load, no telemetry. Link it from the manifest.
  • Content Security Policy on the hosted page, and Office.js as the only external script.
  • Component tests (@testing-library/react + jsdom) for the four panels, and one end-to-end pass through the dev harness in CI.
  • Drop the dev harness from the production bundle, or keep it deliberately as the public demo at a separate path. The second is the better use: a live demo needs no Excel.
  • An error panel with "copy details" so a user can paste what went wrong into an issue.

docs.title: 4. Reach (optional, after 1–3)
docs.text:
• Microsoft Marketplace (AppSource) listing. It is the only route for individuals whose organization blocks sideloading, and it requires validation, a support URL and a privacy policy, which steps 1 and 3 produce.
  • PNG export of the preview, and y-axis percent on proportion charts.
  • Tables that grow: bind live updates to an Excel table so appended rows are picked up, instead of a fixed range.

docs.title: Methods: funnel plots and over-dispersion
docs.text:
This is qikit's record of how its funnel plots are computed, which published method each step follows, and where it deliberately departs from that method and why. The numbered references at the end are the ones cited, as [n], in the docstrings of src/qikit/funnel.py and src/qikit/_funnel/, the core modules they call (core/contours.py, core/dispersion.py, core/pvalues.py, core/power.py, core/dist.py), and the TypeScript twin (excel-addin/packages/engine/src/stats.ts, spc-core.ts).

Time-ordered control charts (qic(): run, I, p, u, Laney p′/u′ and the rest) are recorded in qic-methods.md, with their conformance to qicharts2.

docs.title: 1. Which charts are funnels
docs.text:
Funnels are drawn by funnel(). Its measure= and overdispersion= pick one of six engine charts, whose codes the engine's docstrings and the shared fixtures use:

funnel(...) Engine chart Count model Limits Over-dispersion measure="proportion", overdispersion=False p Binomial Exact binomial [1, A.1.1] Estimated and reported, not applied measure="rate", overdispersion=False u Poisson Exact Poisson, exposure as denominator [1, A.2.1, A.2.3] Estimated and reported, not applied measure="oe", overdispersion=False oe Poisson Exact Poisson on expected events [1, A.2.1] Estimated and reported, not applied measure="proportion" (default overdispersion=True) pp Beta-binomial Exact quantiles of the additive model [1, eq. 11] Additive τ² [1, §5], applied measure="rate" up Poisson–gamma Exact quantiles of the additive model [1, eq. 11; 7] Additive τ² [1, §5], applied measure="oe" oep Poisson–gamma Exact quantiles of the additive model [1, eq. 11; 7] Additive τ² [1, §5], applied

The contours are 99.8% and 95% by default (limits=). within_dispersion= scales any count model for counts that clump within cases (§4.12), and the binomial for the items of one survey (§4.13). qic() keeps p/u with 3σ Shewhart limits and pp/up with Laney's σ_z [6] for time order; it no longer draws funnels.

docs.title: 2. What each chart answers
docs.text:
The two kinds of funnel ask different questions, and both are legitimate:

  • Unadjusted (p, u and oe): is this provider's result consistent with the target, given chance (and, for O/E, the risk model)? A provider in the upper tail of real between-provider variation will flag here, correctly, because it does differ from the target.
  • Adjusted (pp, up and oep): is this provider unusual given the observed spread between providers? This treats the spread, τ, as "acceptable" variation [1, §5] and flags only providers outside it.

funnel(compare_to=) names the two: "model" is the unadjusted chart of O/E against 1.0 (center=1.0, overdispersion=False), and "peers" the adjusted chart around the pooled value (the default settings). A fixed center with the adjustment on answers neither question (§4.2.1).

Which question applies is a policy decision. Make it before seeing the data, and record it in the analysis plan [8, step 1]; Spiegelhalter calls the boundary between acceptable and out-of-control "a matter of judgment" [1, §5]. If the data are over-dispersed, the spread itself is a finding about the system: unmeasured case mix, data or coding differences, or real differences in practice. Spiegelhalter is explicit that adjusting is "purely a temporary measure" while its causes are explored [1, §5]. Every unadjusted funnel therefore reports the estimate (dispersion_phi, dispersion_tau, overdispersed) and, when it is present, a dispersion_note saying so.

At individual-physician volumes the two usually coincide. τ is rarely detectable with 5–20 expected events per physician; on the bundled 24-surgeon data φ̂ = 0.93 and τ̂ = 0. When τ̂ = 0 the adjusted chart is the unadjusted chart, to the bit.

docs.title: 4.1 Exact limits, interpolated
docs.text:
Every funnel draws the exact discrete quantile with Spiegelhalter's continuity interpolation: r_p is the smallest count with F(r_p) ≥ p, and the limit is (r_p − α)/n with α = (F(r_p) − p)/f(r_p) [1, A.1.1]. The normal approximation of eq. 3 is symmetric and badly placed at the volumes individual providers have. At 5 expected events and O/E = 1, the 99.8% limits are:

Method Lower Upper Exact Poisson (qikit) 0.00 2.55 Normal, natural scale (eq. 3) 0 (clipped) 2.38 Normal, square-root scale 0.10 2.86 Normal, log scale 0.25 3.98

The transformed-scale versions flag a zero-death physician (P = 0.7%) or a three-death physician against ten expected (P = 1.0%) as better than expected at the nominal 0.1%. The natural-scale version's upper limit is too tight, so it over-flags high outliers.

R's qpois/qbinom return r_p without the interpolation, so an external cross-check should bracket qikit's value between r_p − 1 and r_p.

The upper contour sits at the exact test's boundary. For an integer count O the interpolated quantile q = r_p − α decides the two sides differently:

  • the point is below the lower contour exactly when P(X ≤ O) < α, which is the exact test;
  • the point is above the upper contour q exactly when P(X > O) < α, which leaves out the probability of the observed count itself.

So qikit draws the upper contour at q + 1 on the count scale (capped at n for a proportion). With that, a point is beyond either contour exactly when its conventional exact p-value, P(X ≥ O) above or P(X ≤ O) below (§4.11), is below the contour's tail probability. The drawn line, p_value, the point's color and, on the unadjusted O/E chart, "the point's Garwood 95% interval excludes the center line" are then one statement. The test suite checks all three on random funnels of every chart.

The model, center line, τ² and levels are Spiegelhalter's; only the drawn upper boundary moves, by at most one count. At 5 expected events and θ₀ = 1 the 99.8% upper limit is 13.77 events (O/E 2.75) rather than the published 12.77 (2.55). Compared with other funnel software that draws the published contour, qikit is up to one count more conservative above the line at small volumes. This is a qikit derivation. As far as we know it is not a published contour, though the test it draws is the standard exact test, and also the comparison of a provider's exact interval with the benchmark.

Shape at small counts. Spiegelhalter's upper contour wiggles at small denominators: on the ratio scale it climbs briefly within every integer step before falling again. Within a step α runs from 1 to 0 as λ = θ₀n grows, and q = r_p − α has slope q′(λ) = 1 + α(r_p/λ − 1), so q/λ has slope proportional to q′λ − q, which is 1 at the start of every step. The contour qikit draws, (q + 1)/λ, has slope proportional to

q′λ − (q + 1) = (1 − α)(λ − r_p − 1),

which is never positive, since an upper quantile r_p is at least λ. So it is monotone by construction, in all four families. On dense grids the published contour climbs back thousands of times (largest climb 0.067 on O/E for E between 0.3 and 2, 0.021 on a proportion at θ₀ = 0.1); the drawn contour never does, and no display smoothing is needed. The lower contours were already monotone.

To start the axis where volumes become informative, use x_range=(2, None) on an O/E funnel or about n = 20 on a proportion, or spread the axis with x_log=True.

docs.title: 4.2 Center line
docs.text: The default is the pooled rate (Σy/Σn, or ΣO/ΣE), which judges providers against their peers and, for O/E, absorbs overall miscalibration of the risk model. center=1.0 judges O/E against the risk model itself. The pooled line includes each provider. On a small cohort, one extreme provider drags the line toward itself, leaves every other provider to one side, and inflates τ̂ even though its own residual is winsorized. This is the circularity [1, §5] attributes to Marshall et al. The test suite pins a case where it hides the provider entirely (test_a_lone_outlier_still_leaks_in_through_the_pooled_center_line). Anchoring with center= removes the effect. Pavlou et al. [9] suggest a pre-specified τ as another remedy (§6).

docs.title: 4.2.1 A fixed center under the adjustment: the absorbed gap
docs.text:
τ̂ is estimated around whatever center line the chart uses. Around the pooled value it measures the spread between providers. Around a fixed center= it also absorbs any system-wide gap between the providers and that center: a whole system running 10% above its risk model looks, to the moment estimator, like providers spread widely around 1.0. Every limit then widens by that gap, and the chart answers neither question of §2. It is not judging against the model, because the allowance has swallowed the gap, and it is not judging against peers, because the line is not theirs.

On 60 simulated physicians' stays (a system running 10% long, three physicians 40% worse on top, within_dispersion="estimate"), the default chart has τ̂ = 0.035 and flags the three. With center=1.0 alone τ̂ rises to 0.136, the limits at the median volume widen by about 112%, and one of the three falls back to an alert. With compare_to="model" (no allowance) 13 physicians are outliers and 23 alerts: the system-wide gap is now visible as signal, which is what that question asks.

The guard. When center= is fixed, overdispersion=True and τ is estimated (not tau=), funnel() compares the providers' pooled value Σnᵢyᵢ/Σnᵢ with the center and warns when both of the following hold:

  1. The gap is beyond chance and the spread between providers: a two-sided p < 0.001 from a t test on K − 1 degrees of freedom with the robust (sandwich) variance K/(K − 1)·Σnᵢ²(yᵢ − ȳ)²/(Σnᵢ)², on the model's nᵢ (÷ φ). The observed scatter carries chance, within-case clumping and real spread together, so the test needs no τ̂. A first version used the model variance ȳ/Σnᵢ + τ̂²Σnᵢ²/(Σnᵢ)² instead. At K = 20 it warned in up to 3.6% of no-gap cohorts, because the published estimator understates τ at small K (§4.3).
  2. The gap matters: the 99.8% half-width at the median provider's volume, √(V₀ + τ̂²) around the fixed center against √(V₀ + τ̂ₚ²) with τ̂ₚ the same estimator around the pooled value, is at least 10% wider.

The warning gives the gap and the widening, and names the fix: compare_to="model" on O/E, overdispersion=False with the target on a proportion or rate, or no center= for the peer question. summary reports center_gap (pooled ÷ center − 1), center_gap_p and tau_pooled. The calibration is in §5.

docs.title: 4.3 The over-dispersion estimator: published by default, debiased on request
docs.text:
overdispersion() in core/dispersion.py implements [1, §5]:

  1. Pearson residuals zᵢ = (yᵢ − θ₀)/√V₀ᵢ, with V₀ᵢ = θ₀/nᵢ for counts and θ₀(1 − θ₀)/nᵢ for proportions (eq. 4).
  2. Winsorize at the 10th and 90th percentiles; φ̂ = mean(z_W²) (eqs. 6, 8).
  3. τ̂² = (Kφ̂ − (K − 1)) / (Σwᵢ − Σwᵢ²/Σwᵢ), wᵢ = 1/V₀ᵢ (eq. 10, the DerSimonian–Laird form [3]), and τ̂² = 0 when φ̂ < (K − 1)/K.

That is the default, tau_method="spiegelhalter", exactly as published. CQC and NHS SHMI run the same uncorrected method of moments on a transformed scale instead; "cqc" and "shmi" reproduce those, as FunnelPlotR [13] does (§4.17).

The consistency factor. Winsorizing a standard normal at its p and 1 − p quantiles z = Φ⁻¹(1 − p) leaves E[Z_W²] = (1 − 2p) − 2z·φ(z) + 2p·z², which is 0.6787 at p = 0.10. Spiegelhalter derives the correction c(p) = 1/E[Z_W²] = 1.4735 (eq. 9), but reports that it gave "somewhat wide limits" and does not adopt it in his example. tau_method="winsorized" applies it: φ̂ = c(0.10)·mean(z_W²).

Which to use, and why the published one is the default. Without the factor, φ̂ averages 0.68 under pure chance, so the τ² = 0 gate needs a true over-dispersion of about 1.47 before it moves. Small real spreads between providers are then ignored, the adjusted limits stay at their unadjusted width, and more providers flag. The table below (200 replicates of K = 1,000 providers, E ~ U(2, 60), Poisson counts with true relative spread τ) shows the size of the effect:

true τ φ̂ published τ̂ published τ̂ debiased τ̂ plain DL (no winsorizing) 0 0.678 0 0.017 0.016 0.10 0.881 0 in every replicate 0.098 0.100 0.20 1.452 0.120 0.192 0.200 0.30 2.387 0.212 0.285 0.300 0.10, plus 2% gross outliers (O/E 2.5) 0.942 0.004 0.113 0.230

The two estimators answer the screening question differently:

  • The published estimator is the more sensitive screen. It flags more providers whose difference is the ordinary spread between peers (§5: 0.54% of in-distribution providers beyond the 99.8% line at K = 150, τ = 0.3, against a nominal 0.1%), and it finds a planted outlier more often (70% against 38% there). qikit 0.10 made the debiased estimator the default; in production use at physician scale it was not sensitive enough for screening, so 1.0 restores the published one. It is also uncorrected, as the CQC, NHS and FunnelPlotR estimators are, so its flag rates are comparable with theirs.
  • The debiased estimator holds the stated chance-flag rate. Use tau_method="winsorized" when flags are acted on individually and the 0.1% and 2.5% in expected_false_flags must mean what they say, as on a large funnel feeding credentialing. It stays robust to the outliers being screened for: plain DerSimonian–Laird doubles τ̂ when 2% of providers are gross outliers, the winsorized estimators do not.

funnel_sensitivity() runs a funnel under each τ option and marks the providers whose tier depends on the choice; a flag that does is a judgment to make explicitly.

A center line fixed in advance. Equation 10 counts K − 1 degrees of freedom because θ₀ is estimated from the same providers. With center= given (O/E against 1.0, say) no mean is estimated, and the method-of-moments estimate is τ̂² = K(φ̂ − 1)/Σwᵢ, 0 when φ̂ ≤ 1. "winsorized" uses that form; the published methods keep theirs, since reproducing a published funnel is their purpose. Note also that a fixed center absorbs any overall gap between the cohort and the benchmark into τ̂ (§4.2).

Reproducing published funnels. The default gives the published estimator bit for bit; the shared Python/TypeScript fixtures that check Spiegelhalter's numbers pin it, and funnel_oep_winsorized, funnel_pp_winsorized and funnel_up_winsorized check "winsorized" in both engines. summary["phi"] is the dispersion ratio as the chosen method defines it (c·mean(z_W²) under "winsorized"). On the bundled example (data/examples/physician_mortality_oe.csv, three years pooled) τ̂ is 0 under the default and 0.113 debiased, and the same three physicians are outliers either way.

Pearson rather than square-root residuals. qikit 0.4's oep used the square-root scale, 2(√O − √(θ₀E)), as the CQC variant does, on the grounds that Pearson residuals are skewed at small counts. After winsorizing, the difference is negligible at physician volumes: simulated τ̂ is within 0.015 of the square-root variant, and the bundled surgeons give τ̂ = 0 either way. The natural scale is [1]'s, and it feeds eq. 11 directly, with no delta-method mapping.

docs.title: 4.4 Additive, not multiplicative
docs.text:
Spiegelhalter presents both models and illustrates the difference in his Figure 6. Multiplicative φ inflates every provider's variance by the same factor, so the band keeps closing onto θ₀ at high volume. Additive τ² adds a constant between-provider variance, so the band is "essentially independent of volume" there [1, §5]. His companion paper finds the additive formulation has the stronger conceptual foundation [2], and it is what CQC, NHS SHMI and FunnelPlotR use. Pavlou et al. [9] reach the same preference for random-effects approaches when the common-mean assumption fails.

For physician comparisons the choice matters at both ends of the funnel:

  • Small volume. V₀ dominates, and additive τ² barely moves the limits. Multiplicative φ widens them most, in absolute terms, exactly where power is already 5–44%.
  • Large volume. Additive limits level off at roughly θ₀ ± z·τ, so a busy provider is not flagged for a difference smaller than the spread between providers.

qikit 0.4's multiplicative oep had a further defect. When φ̂ was clamped to 1 it still drew normal-approximation limits, 7–10% tighter than oe at E ≤ 8. Switching to oep "to be safe" therefore produced more high flags. In 0.5, oep with τ̂ = 0 is oe.

docs.title: 4.5 Adjusted limits drawn exactly
docs.text:
Eq. 11 describes a model in which providers' true rates θᵢ are spread around θ₀ with variance τ², and observed counts are Poisson or binomial given θᵢ. Drawing θᵢ from a gamma distribution (counts) or a beta distribution (proportions) with that mean and variance gives the classic hierarchical model for standardized ratios [7], whose marginal distributions are exact:

Family Count distribution Variance on the indicator scale Counts (up and oep) Poisson–gamma (negative binomial), size θ₀²/τ² θ₀/n + τ² (eq. 11 exactly) Proportions (pp) Beta-binomial, α + β = θ₀(1 − θ₀)/τ² − 1 θ₀(1 − θ₀)/n + τ²(n − 1)/n

qikit draws the interpolated quantiles of these, as §4.1 does for the unadjusted ones. This is the one methodological departure from [1]: same model and same variance, exact rather than normal quantiles. It is the substitution [1, Appendix A] itself makes for the unadjusted limits. Neither Verburg et al. [8] nor Pavlou et al. [9] evaluate it. Verburg uses multiplicative φ̂ because the additive model could not be combined with exact binomial limits. Pavlou uses the additive model on the log scale and accepts the normal approximation, warning that it may fail at small counts. The mixture distributions remove that trade-off.

Implementation notes (dist.py, stats.ts):

  • Arithmetic only. Each pmf is built from its term ratio f(k+1)/f(k) outward from the mode and normalized at the end. It uses only + − × ÷, so results are bit-identical across platforms and between Python and TypeScript. There is no lgamma cancellation as τ² → 0, and the cost scales with the distribution's spread, not its mean.
  • Validated against scipy.stats (binom, nbinom, betabinom) to < 1e-9, and one beta-binomial case against 60-digit mpmath. There scipy itself is off by ~1e-5, from the cancellation this design avoids.
  • Fallbacks. A spread no beta distribution can have (τ² ≥ θ₀(1 − θ₀)), or a distribution too wide to walk (only absurd τ), falls back to eq. 11 as published, with a proportion's contours kept between 0 and 1. summary["limit_method"] then says "normal" instead of "exact". A non-integer denominator is interpolated between its whole neighbors (§4.13), and limit_method says "interpolated".
  • Computation. From 0.10 the walk is vectorized in blocks after its first 64 terms, with the upward and downward running products done by np.multiply.accumulate and np.divide.accumulate and every sum by np.cumsum. All three are strictly sequential, so every term, the point where the walk stops, every tail sum, and therefore every limit and p-value are bit-identical to the scalar loop the TypeScript twin keeps (checked on 36,000 random calls across all four families). A walk, and each Poisson mean inversion, is cached per distribution, because a point's two contours and its p-value walk the same pmf. A 1,000-provider oep funnel at hospital volumes (E from 30 to 2,000) takes about 0.3 s cold, down from 1.3 s, and 0.06 s when the same distributions recur. scipy is not used. It is not a dependency, its incomplete-gamma and beta routines differ from this walk in the last ulps across platforms, and its beta-binomial loses about 1e-5 to the cancellation described above. The cold time is dominated by the lgamma-based Poisson mean inversion behind intervals and detectability. Solving all providers' inversions at once would make it faster, but it moves the last quantized digit of some results at counts in the thousands, so it has not been done.

docs.title: 4.6 Laney's p′/u′ stay for time order
docs.text: Laney's σ_z is the mean moving range of consecutive standardized residuals [6]. That statistic depends on order and is defined for time series [11]. In a funnel the order is the sort by volume. On the bundled 3-year surgeon data, the published test finds no over-dispersion, yet the 0.4 up funnel widened its limits 1.87× and hid all three real signals. Since 0.5 a funnel uses the additive method, and Laney's pp/up remain only as time-ordered charts in qic().

docs.title: 4.7 Warn tier and multiplicity
docs.text: The 99.8% contour marks outliers and the 95% contour alerts (the signal column: "outlier", "alert" or "none"). The tiers never overlap, and alerts are counted in n_alert, apart from n_outlier, because at one chance alert in forty per side a large funnel would always report one. About 0.1% of average providers land beyond each 99.8% line, roughly one in a 1,000-provider one-sided funnel, and 2.5% beyond each 95% line, about 24 there. summary["expected_false_flags"] reports those numbers for the chart, so an alert count is read against them. [1, §6] recommends formal FDR control [12] carried out separately from the plot. Every funnel reports Benjamini–Hochberg q-values, and signal="fdr" flags by them (§4.11).

docs.title: 4.8 Power and intervals
docs.text:
Not part of [1]. At physician volumes a funnel mostly cannot detect even a doubling of risk [10], and a blank funnel reads as a clean bill of health. This is in the spirit of Verburg's sample-size step [8, step 3], with a doubling rather than 1.5× as the reference effect. Power is fixed at 80% and is not a parameter: on a chart that feeds credentialing, a tunable threshold invites reporting whichever number reads best.

The detectable effect. It is measured against the limit the chart actually draws, including the wider limits of oep/pp/up: the question is whether this point would flag on this chart. Signals fire strictly above ucl, so a count flags when X ≥ ⌊ucl·n⌋ + 1. The smallest true effect with 80% power is the one at which F(⌊ucl·n⌋) = 0.2. With the upper contour at the exact test's boundary (§4.1) that event is exactly "p < 0.001". The equation is solved exactly in the CDF's own parameter, never by scanning over ratios. funnel() reports the result as min_detectable and the interval as ci_lower/ci_upper on every measure:

Engine chart Count model Solved for Engine column (y scale) Per-point 95% CI oe, oep Poisson(ρE) mean, then ρ = μ/E min_detectable_oe Garwood [5] u, up funnel Poisson(θn) mean, then θ = μ/n min_detectable Garwood [5] p, pp funnel Binomial(n, θ) θ directly min_detectable Clopper–Pearson [14]

A u funnel's algebra is the O/E chart's with exposure in place of expected events, so it reuses the same functions. A Clopper–Pearson interval inverts the exact binomial test the same way Garwood inverts the Poisson one: the lower bound is the θ at which x or more events has probability 0.025, and the upper bound is the θ at which x or fewer does.

The Poisson solve takes safeguarded Newton steps on log F, where F = f·S, S is a running sum of products of j/μ, and d log F/dμ = −1/S. Six to ten steps replace fifty full CDF sweeps. A thousand-provider funnel with counts in the thousands (length of stay in days) took about 17 s by bisection and now takes well under 1 s. The TypeScript engine still bisects; the two agree far inside the quantization below.

Cross-platform reproducibility. The Poisson solve uses one lgamma, whose last ulp differs between platforms, so it is quantized to 1e-9. The binomial solve is lgamma-free. Its CDF is built from the term ratio outward from the mode, using the same walk as the binomial limits (§4.5), and normalized by its own total, so (1 − θ)ⁿ, which underflows at hospital volumes, is never formed. The walk uses only + − × ÷. The θ solve takes safeguarded Newton steps on the log of the smaller tail from a Wilson-score start, about five CDF evaluations instead of fifty, and stops once a step is below 1e-13 of θ. A proportion funnel of 5,000 providers fell from 10 s to about 1 s. The TypeScript engine still bisects; the two agree to about 1e-13 relative. Contours, which must sit exactly on the test, keep their own bisection and are bit-identical across engines.

The summary. Every chart reports underpowered, n_underpowered and, when underpowered, a quotable power_note. Ghosted (exclude=) points are left out: they cannot flag, so they say nothing about the chart's reach.

  • O/E. The test is min_detectable_oe > 2, with the median reported as min_detectable_oe_median.
  • p/u funnels. A proportion or rate has no natural unit, so the test is relative to the center line: min_detectable / cl > 2, with the median of that ratio reported as min_detectable_ratio_median. On a p funnel with cl ≥ 0.5 a doubling is not a proportion. There only points that cannot flag at all count as underpowered; the ratio still says how far above the line a point would have to be.

Edge cases. A point whose limit reaches n cannot flag at any θ. Internally its detectable proportion is infinite, so it counts as underpowered and enters the median; the column shows NaN. With exact interpolated limits this is effectively unreachable. A non-integer denominator (n/φ under within_dispersion, or an averaged n) has no binomial description. Its detectability and interval are interpolated between the whole neighbors, as its limits are (§4.13).

docs.title: 4.9 The volume axis
docs.text:
[1, §2] plots each indicator against its precision ρ = 1/s², with the limits drawn as smooth contours. qikit plots against the denominator instead: sample size on p/pp, exposure on u/up, and expected events on oe/oep. That is the same axis up to a constant. For a proportion s² = θ₀(1 − θ₀)/n, so ρ ∝ n. For a rate or an O/E ratio s² = θ₀/n (or θ₀/E), so ρ ∝ n (or E). The difference is that volume is a unit a reader already understands. The adjusted funnels use the same axis, which is where the levelling-off of §4.4 shows.

This is the axis funnel() draws. A funnel whose denominators are all equal falls back to plotting by unit, because a volume axis would stack every point on one line. The y axis is fitted to the providers, the center line and each contour's value nearest the center line, so the low-volume flare does not set the scale.

The contours. FunnelResult.limits() evaluates the limits on about 200 geometric steps between the smallest and largest denominator, merged with every point's own n. It calls the same limit functions on the same path as the per-point limits (core.contours.funnel_contours), with the unrounded τ², so each curve passes exactly through the limit that decided that point's signal. A drawn point can therefore never sit inside the curve while being flagged, or outside it while not being flagged. A test pins this bit-for-bit on every funnel fixture. Between grid steps the plot interpolates linearly.

Binomial charts step in whole numbers. On p/pp the grid is rounded to integers, where the limits are exact. A non-integer n is interpolated between its whole neighbors (§4.13), so the contours stay continuous through every step, including under within_dispersion, where the model sees n/φ. The Poisson and Poisson–gamma charts take any positive n.

Log scale. x_log=True log-scales the axis, which spreads out a funnel whose providers span orders of magnitude. Plotly takes an annotation's position on a log axis as log10 of the value, so the center-line and limit labels and the signal labels are placed on that scale.

docs.title: 4.10 One-sided signalling
docs.text:
Many indicators matter in one direction only; excess mortality is the usual example. funnel(worse="higher") flags only points beyond the upper contours, and worse="lower" only those beyond the lower ones. worse=None, the default, is the two-sided chart of [1]. The filter applies to both tiers, and through them to the point colors, the legend ("Worse than expected: …"), the counts and label_signals=. summary["worse"] records it.

  • Each side keeps its own tail probability. A one-sided chart flags at 0.1% and 2.5% per provider by chance, half the two-sided chart's 0.2% and 5%.
  • The other side's limits are still drawn, because they are still where the null model puts them. Hide them with styles={"lcl": {"visible": False}, "lcl_95": {"visible": False}}.
  • Only on funnels. Runs rules describe patterns, not points beyond a line, and are never side-filtered, so qic() has no side argument.
